questions.question: What chemical substance makes up the genetic material in living organisms?
options: Protein
DNA
Starch
Lipid

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the basic structure of a DNA molecule?
options: It consists of a single linear protein chain
It is made of two chains of smaller chemical units joined together
It is a ring of linked glucose molecules
It is a branched network of fatty acids

questions.question: What term refers to all of the DNA contained within an individual cell?
options: Proteome
Genome
Nucleolus
Phenotype

questions.question: How are the chemical chains arranged in a standard model of DNA?
options: Spiralled around each other in a double helix with cross links
Aligned in flat parallel lines with no middle connections
Folded randomly into a spherical bundle
Linked end-to-end to form one continuous line

questions.question: Why is extracted DNA sometimes visible to the naked eye during a laboratory experiment?
options: Extracted DNA expands to ten times its normal width
Individual DNA molecules clump together when a large amount is extracted
DNA reacts with air to emit visible light
Extraction changes DNA into a solid mineral crystal

questions.question: What is the typical visual appearance of DNA after it has been extracted from fruit tissue?
options: A bright green liquid
A white, stringy or slimy precipitate
Fine black powder
Hard metallic crystals

questions.question: Which statement about genomes in different living species is correct?
options: Only animals possess a genome
All organisms have a genome, showing both similarities and differences across species
Every species shares an identical genome
Bacteria do not contain a genome

questions.question: What are the tightly-packed structures formed when DNA is wound up inside cells called?
options: Ribosomes
Chromosomes
Chloroplasts
Mitochondria

questions.question: How many pairs of chromosomes are found in human body cells, and where are they stored?
options: 46 pairs stored in the cytoplasm
23 pairs stored in the nucleus
23 single chromosomes stored in the cell wall
12 pairs stored in the nucleus

questions.question: What are the specific sections of DNA in chromosomes that store instructions for inherited features called?
options: Genes
Enzymes
Hormones
Antibodies

questions.question: What role does non-coding DNA play in an organism's genetic material?
options: It generates chemical energy for cell movement
It contains instructions controlling when information in genes is used
It forms the protective outer wall of plant cells
It breaks down waste products inside the cytoplasm

questions.question: Where is genetic material located inside plant, animal, and fungi cells?
options: Cell membrane
Cytoplasm
Nucleus
Vacuole

questions.question: Where do bacterial cells store their genetic material?
options: Inside a nucleus
In the cytoplasm
Inside chloroplasts
Attached to the outer cell wall

questions.question: What is heredity?
options: The process of breaking down food for energy
The process of passing on genetic features from organisms to their offspring
The process of absorbing nutrients from the environment
The physical movement of cells during growth

questions.question: Why do offspring typically show family resemblance to both parents?
options: They inherit genetic material from both parents
They choose which physical traits to copy
They eat the same diet as their parents
They are exposed to identical climate conditions

questions.question: Why are non-identical offspring from the same parents usually not completely identical to each other?
options: They inherit different combinations of genetic material from their parents
Only one child inherits genetic material while others do not
DNA changes completely every year after birth
Genetic material is passed on only to the firstborn child

questions.question: Which characteristics can be inherited by offspring?
options: Characteristics caused by physical injuries
Characteristics caused by instructions in genetic material
Skills learned through repeated practice
Skin tanning caused by sun exposure

questions.question: Why are features caused by lifestyle or the environment unable to be passed to offspring?
options: They are not stored as instructions in the genetic material
They are too small to be transferred
Offspring automatically repair all environmental changes
Lifestyle features are lost during adulthood

questions.question: Which feature is an example of an inherited characteristic?
options: A scar on a leg
Natural eye colour
A spoken accent
A body tattoo

questions.question: Which experimental method was used by Rosalind Franklin's team in 1952 to produce an image of DNA?
options: Light microscopy
X-ray diffraction
Computer modelling
Chemical staining with iodine
